Portfolio Rebalancing and Transaction Costs


                        Asset    Target Weight     After Market Gains
                        Stocks        40%            50% (too high)
                        Bonds         60%             50% (too low)

    • Target allocation: The client’s risk capacity and investment horizon determine the
      stock–bond mix. A return forecast is optional.

    • Rebalancing: In this example, sell stocks worth 10% of portfolio value and buy the same
      amount of bonds to restore the target, before costs.

    • The Class 5 cost calculation: At an assumed 10 bp per purchase or sale, cost is
      0.001 × (0.10 + 0.10) = 0.02%, or 2 bp of portfolio value. More frequent rebalancing
      can increase this cost.

Multiple-Choice Question: Recovery after Ransomware



   A payment firm keeps live records and backups under the same administrator account. An
   attacker takes over that account and encrypts both copies.

   Which change most directly improves the firm’s ability to recover?

    A) Maintain separately protected backups and test restoration regularly.

    B) Replicate records more often under the same administrator account.

    C) Encrypt the live database more strongly under the same access rules.

   D) Retain more login alerts without changing how backups are protected.

A Customer Matches a Sanctions-List Name



   Illustrative account application: the name matches a list entry, but the date of birth differs.

    • The bank’s problem. It needs to establish whether the applicant and the listed person
      are the same person.

    • The software’s task. Compare names and identifiers, find possible matches, and show
      the evidence to a reviewer.

    • The reviewer’s task. Resolve missing or conflicting information and record the decision.

   Regulatory technology (RegTech) helps institutions perform and document these checks.

WeLab Case: A Similar Name Creates an Alert



   Hypothetical applicant: the name resembles a sanctions entry, the date of birth differs, and
   the identity number is not yet verified.

    • Compare the matching and conflicting identifiers against source records.

    • Verify the missing evidence and keep a record of what resolves the uncertainty.

    • Apply the bank’s screening rules; record the decision and escalate unresolved doubt.

   Review capacity: if 40 alerts remain and staff can review 10 today, 30 need a priority and
   interim-control decision. AI summaries can assist review without settling the identity question.

sample_text.37:
LLM-Extracted Filings as Return Predictors


   Illustrative filing: Revenue rose from HK$100 million to HK$120 million.

                             Revenue growth = 120/100 − 1 = 20%.



    • Extraction: The LLM records the amounts and reporting periods. Check the units and
      retain the source passage before calculating growth.

    • Timing (Class 1): The predictor becomes available when the company publishes the
      information, not at the accounting period end.

    • Evaluation (Classes 2–4): Test whether the extracted predictor improves forecasts on
      later observations relative to the same model without it.
